new.title: Walk around the fan-shaped Karlsruhe Palace
new.desc: Karlsruhe Palace was founded in 1715 by Margrave Karl Wilhelm of Baden-Durlach, and the city's streets radiate from its tower like a fan. Today it houses the Badisches Landesmuseum with Turkish booty and Baden regional history.
new.tip: Climb the palace tower for a view of the fan layout; the surrounding Schlossgarten is free.

new.title: See the Pyramid, Karlsruhe's founding tomb
new.desc: The sandstone pyramid on the Marktplatz marks the tomb of city founder Margrave Karl Wilhelm (d. 1738). Built in 1823-25 by Friedrich Weinbrenner, it replaced a wooden predecessor and is the city's emblem.
new.tip: The tomb chamber can be viewed from inside; the Marktplatz is atmospheric in the evening.

new.title: Stroll the Botanical Garden and its glass houses
new.desc: The Botanischer Garten beside the palace dates to 1853 and has historic tropical glasshouses. Admission to the grounds is free.
new.tip: Glasshouses have shorter hours than the park (Tuesday to Friday daytime); check before going.

new.title: Explore media art at the ZKM
new.desc: The Zentrum für Kunst und Medien opened in 1997 in a former munitions factory building from 1918. It combines the Museum für Neue Kunst and the Medienmuseum, with interactive digital art.
new.tip: Allow two to three hours; weekends are popular.
new.q: ZKM Zentrum für Kunst und Medien, Lorenzstraße 19, 76135 Karlsruhe

new.title: Visit the Majolika ceramics workshop
new.desc: The Majolika Manufaktur, founded in 1901 on the initiative of Grand Duke Friedrich I, still produces hand-painted art ceramics in the palace garden. A museum shows historic pieces.
new.tip: Check workshop viewing hours; the shop stocks tiles and tableware.

new.title: Climb the Turmberg tower above Durlach
new.desc: The Turmberg (256 m) carries the medieval keep of a castle of the Margraves of Baden, now an observation tower. The view takes in Karlsruhe, the Rhine plain and the Palatinate hills.
new.tip: Take the Turmbergbahn funicular up and walk down the Hexenstäffele.

new.title: Admire Old Masters at the Staatliche Kunsthalle
new.desc: Founded in 1846, the Kunsthalle holds one of Germany's best collections of German, French and Dutch painting, including Grünewald's Crucifixion. The neo-Renaissance building is by Heinrich Hübsch.
new.tip: Check the website for free-entry days.

new.title: Meet the fossils at the Naturkundemuseum
new.desc: The Staatliches Museum für Naturkunde Karlsruhe has a Vivarium with live reptiles and fish and fossils from the Upper Rhine region. It was founded in 1785 and moved to its present building in 1872.
new.tip: Family friendly; the Vivarium is the highlight.
new.q: Staatliches Museum für Naturkunde Karlsruhe, Erbprinzenstraße 13, 76133 Karlsruhe

new.title: Discover Karlsburg Palace in Durlach
new.desc: Schloss Karlsburg was built from the 1690s for Margrave Friedrich Magnus after Durlach was destroyed in 1689. It was the seat of Baden-Durlach before the court moved to Karlsruhe, and today holds the Pfinzgaumuseum.
new.tip: Combine with a walk through Durlach's old town.

new.title: See Gottesaue Palace and its concert hall
new.desc: Schloss Gottesaue is a Renaissance palace of 1588-97, rebuilt after World War II and now home to the Hochschule für Musik. A modern concert hall was added in 2015.
new.tip: Student concerts take place in term time; check the website.

new.title: Step inside the Protestant Stadtkirche
new.desc: Friedrich Weinbrenner's classicist Evangelische Stadtkirche (1807-16) stands opposite the Rathaus on the Marktplatz. It is one of the key buildings of his planned city.
new.tip: Often open in the daytime; combine with the Pyramide.

new.title: Look at Germany's Constitutional Court building
new.desc: The Bundesverfassungsgericht has sat in Karlsruhe since 1951, and its glass-and-steel courtroom building of 1969 is a landmark of postwar architecture.
new.tip: Book a guided visit in advance; the grounds can be seen from outside.

new.title: See the Hoepfner Burg brewery castle
new.desc: The Hoepfner Burg is a castle-style brewery building of 1898 built for the brewer Hoepfner. The Hoepfner family brewery is still based on the site.
new.tip: Look at the building from the street; the Burghof restaurant is open to visitors.

new.title: Try beef roulade at Zum Kleinen Ketterer
new.desc: This traditional Baden Gasthaus in the city centre reopened in 2026 with a menu of home-style regional dishes. Beef roulade with red cabbage and spätzle is a signature plate.
new.tip: Reserve for dinner; it is within walking distance of the Marktplatz.

new.title: Drink house-brewed beer at Deutscher Kaiser
new.desc: The Brauerei-Gasthaus Deutscher Kaiser in Karlsruhe-Neureut brews its own beers and serves Baden dishes in a classic brewery tavern. Over 40 schnapps are on offer.
new.tip: Try the house beer with a schnitzel; the tram reaches Neureut.
new.q: Brauerei-Gasthaus Deutscher Kaiser, Teutschneureuter Straße 30, Neureut, 76149 Karlsruhe

new.title: Taste local beer at Brauhaus Kühler Krug
new.desc: Kühler Krug is a Karlsruhe brewhouse listed by the city tourism site for its own brewed beers and hearty food.
new.tip: Order the house beers with a Brauhaus plate.
new.q: Brauhaus Kühler Krug, Wilhelm-Baur-Straße 3a, Weststadt, 76135 Karlsruhe

new.title: Sip beer at the Alte Durlacher Brauerei
new.desc: The Alte Durlacher Brauerei is a brewery pub in Durlach's old town serving its own beers with Baden dishes. Durlach is the historic seat of the margraves of Baden-Durlach.
new.tip: Visit after the Karlsburg or Turmberg.
new.q: Alte Durlacher Brauerei, Pfinztalstraße 33, Durlach, 76227 Karlsruhe

new.title: Eat at the Erste Fracht Braugasthaus
new.desc: Erste Fracht is a Karlsruhe brewery pub combining traditional German hospitality with craft-beer flair. It serves house beers alongside regional dishes.
new.tip: Reserve at weekends.

new.title: Sip an espresso at Espresso Tostino
new.desc: Espresso Tostino is a small coffee roastery cafe in the Alter Schlachthof creative quarter. It opens weekdays 10-18 and Sunday afternoons.
new.tip: Combine with the Tollhaus and the studios of the old slaughterhouse grounds.

new.title: Have a flat white at Kaffee-Basis
new.desc: Kaffee-Basis is a specialty coffee spot in Karlsruhe's Innenstadt praised by the city tourism board for its coffee and cosy atmosphere.
new.tip: Quiet in the morning; take it with a slice of cake.

new.title: Order an Italian espresso at Espressobar Ostermeier
new.desc: The Espressobar in the southern Waldstraße brings Italian coffee-bar flair to Karlsruhe, with an espresso counter and cakes. The city tourism board lists it as a local favourite.
new.tip: Stand at the bar like in Italy; weekday mornings are busiest.

new.title: Have schnitzel at Gasthaus Karl
new.desc: Gasthaus Karl is a traditional neighbourhood Gasthaus with schnitzel, bratwurst and sauerkraut at moderate prices of about 10-20 euros.
new.tip: Good value; ask for the daily special.

new.title: Meet at Café Palaver for coffee
new.desc: Café Palaver in the Steinstraße is an independent cafe popular with students and architects. It serves coffee, snacks and cake.
new.tip: Quiet in the afternoon; a good place to read.

new.title: Ride the Turmbergbahn funicular
new.desc: The Turmbergbahn has run since 1888 and is among Germany's oldest funiculars, climbing the Turmberg from Durlach in a couple of minutes.
new.tip: Tickets are sold at the station; combine with the Turmberg viewpoint.

new.title: Climb the 528 Hexenstäffele steps
new.desc: The Hexenstäffele is a stone stairway of 528 steps leading from Durlach up the Turmberg slope. It is a popular workout for locals.
new.tip: Bring water; the climb takes about 20 minutes.

new.title: Spend a day at the Zoologischer Stadtgarten
new.desc: Opened in 1865, the Zoologischer Stadtgarten combines a city park and zoo with around 6,500 animals in more than 340 species, including polar bears and sea lions.
new.tip: The park also suits a walk with a lake and rose garden.
new.q: Zoologischer Stadtgarten Karlsruhe, Ettlinger Straße 6, 76137 Karlsruhe

new.title: Walk or picnic in the Schlossgarten
new.desc: The Schlossgarten behind the palace is a landscaped park with cycle paths leading into the Hardtwald forest.
new.tip: Free to enter; the forest starts beyond the lawns.

new.title: Swim at the Rappenwört Rhine beach
new.desc: The Rheinstrandbad Rappenwört on the Altrhein has a lake and sandy shore beside the Rhine floodplain forest. It is a popular summer spot.
new.tip: Summer only; take the tram and a short walk through the forest.

new.title: Browse the Christkindlesmarkt in the centre
new.desc: The Karlsruher Christkindlesmarkt is the city's Christmas market in the Innenstadt, with wooden stalls selling crafts and food such as Glühwein.
new.tip: Visit in the evening when the lights are on; open late November to late December.

new.title: Catch a Karlsruher SC match at the Wildpark
new.desc: Karlsruher SC play at the Wildparkstadion, the club's home since 1955. The stadium has been undergoing rebuilding.
new.tip: Check match dates and current ground; tickets via the club.

new.title: Picnic in the Günther-Klotz-Anlage
new.desc: The Günther-Klotz-Anlage is a large park in the south of the city with lawns and a lake, popular with locals for barbecues and sport.
new.tip: Free to enter; bring a blanket.

new.title: Watch a gig at the Tollhaus
new.desc: The Tollhaus in the Alter Schlachthof is Karlsruhe's cultural centre for cabaret, concerts and children's theatre, in a converted slaughterhouse.
new.tip: Check the programme; the courtyard hosts summer concerts.

new.title: Swim at the Europabad
new.desc: The Europabad is Karlsruhe's large public spa and pool complex with pools and saunas, a short trip from the city centre.
new.tip: Combine a swim with a sauna visit in winter.

new.title: See the Stiftskirche, oldest church in town
new.desc: The late-Gothic Stiftskirche Mariä Himmelfahrt sits on the Marktplatz and contains tombs of the margraves of Baden. Its origins go back to Roman times.
new.tip: Free to enter; the Marktplatz outside has a Baroque ensemble.

new.title: Drink thermal water in the Trinkhalle
new.desc: The Trinkhalle of 1839-42 by Heinrich Hübsch is a neoclassical hall lined with frescoes of Black Forest legends. The warm, salty thermal water can be sampled from a tap.
new.tip: Free; the water tastes strongly of salt.

new.title: Tour the Casino in the Kurhaus
new.desc: The Casino Baden-Baden opened in 1824 in a Kurhaus by Friedrich Weinbrenner. Its opulent salons inspired Dostoevsky and are often called among the most beautiful casinos in the world.
new.tip: Guided tours run daily in the morning.

new.title: See the Festspielhaus, Germany's biggest opera house
new.desc: The Festspielhaus Baden-Baden opened in 1998 in the former railway station and seats 2,500. It hosts international opera and the Berlin Philharmonic Easter Festival.
new.tip: Tours are available on request; check the programme.
new.q: Festspielhaus Baden-Baden, Beim Alten Bahnhof 2, 76530 Baden-Baden

new.title: Look at modern art in the Museum Frieder Burda
new.desc: Richard Meier's white glass-and-steel museum of 2004 holds Frieder Burda's collection of about 1,000 works including Picasso, Richter and Baselitz. It sits in the Lichtentaler Allee park.
new.tip: Walk across the bridge to the Staatliche Kunsthalle next door.
new.q: Museum Frieder Burda, Lichtentaler Allee 8b, 76530 Baden-Baden

new.title: See the Russian Orthodox Church
new.desc: The Russian Church of Baden-Baden was built in 1881-82 for the Russian aristocracy who frequented the spa town. Its golden onion dome is a local landmark.
new.tip: Open on certain days; modest dress required.

new.title: Explore the Roman Bath Ruins
new.desc: The Römische Badruinen under the Friedrichsbad show the hypocaust heating system of the Roman Aquae Aureliae. They were uncovered during 19th-century construction.
new.tip: Visits are by guided tour in season.

new.title: Eat Baden dishes at Weinstube Baldreit
new.desc: Weinstube im Baldreit in the old town holds a Michelin Plate for traditional home cooking. It serves regional Baden wines and dishes.
new.tip: Reserve ahead; it is small and popular.

new.title: Try Baden home cooking at Schneider's Weinstube
new.desc: Schneider's Weinstube im Badener Weinkeller serves Baden cooking listed as grandmother-style cuisine, with local Baden wines.
new.tip: Order a glass of Baden Riesling.
new.q: Schneider's Weinstube im Badener Weinkeller, Maria-Victoria-Straße 2, 76530 Baden-Baden

new.title: Have cake at Café König
new.desc: Café König is a Konditorei with a history of more than 250 years, offering breakfast, light lunch and cakes, with a chocolate and macaron shop attached.
new.tip: Try the Black Forest cherry cake.

new.title: Eat at Fritz & Felix in Brenners Park
new.desc: Fritz & Felix is a restaurant inside Brenners Park-Hotel & Spa with a casual-chic setting and seasonal cooking.
new.tip: Lunch is the more affordable option.
new.q: Fritz & Felix, Brenners Park-Hotel, Schillerstraße 6, 76530 Baden-Baden

new.title: Take the Roman-Irish bath at Friedrichsbad
new.desc: Friedrichsbad opened in 1877 and its Roman-Irish ritual leads bathers through 17 stations of hot air and steam in a Neo-Renaissance setting. Bathing is clothes-free on most days.
new.tip: Allow about three hours; some days are mixed-gender.

new.title: Soak in thermal pools at Caracalla Therme
new.desc: Caracalla Therme opened in 1985 and has indoor and outdoor thermal pools and saunas fed by Baden-Baden's springs. Swimwear is worn in the pools.
new.tip: Stay until evening for the outdoor pool.

new.title: Ride the Merkur funicular to the summit
new.desc: The Merkurbergbahn is Germany's longest and steepest funicular, climbing the Merkur in about five minutes. A viewing tower gives views to the Rhine plain and Vosges.
new.tip: Walk down via the forest path in good weather.

new.title: Stroll the Lichtentaler Allee
new.desc: The Lichtentaler Allee is a 2.3 km park promenade along the Oos river, with rare trees and the Gönneranlage rose garden. It begins near the Kurhaus.
new.tip: Best in spring for rhododendrons and in June for roses.

new.title: Hike to the Teufelskanzel lookout
new.desc: The Teufelskanzel is a rock viewpoint above Baden-Baden with a panorama of the town and the Rhine plain.
new.tip: Wear proper shoes; allow a couple of hours return.
